narrative.what_i_did: Cleaned up the carpenter's ceremonial debris and rewrote the doctrine to describe the actual minimal reinforcing loop the operator named. The operator opened this session in voice with one paragraph: the only thing the carpenter should do is fire a SessionStart hook to check the main tip and ground against the code, do the real work, fire a Stop hook that writes one comms file to itself and to Commander, and repeat. Everything else gets cut. The prior carpenter's hand-off had flagged exactly this hygiene debt under four items, so the cut was scoped and ready. One consolidated commit landed five surgical changes plus this close-out flush. First, CLAUDE.md's doctrine block was rewritten end to end. The old block ran roughly three hundred lines and documented the retired five-file comms protocol (appcommander/comms/current.json, interactions.jsonl, in-flight.jsonl, carpenter-opinions.md, carpenter-state-for-foreman.md), the 10D record schema, the deferred-flush six-event live-comms protocol, the three-section report under PFOR-014, the foreman-handoff file under PFOR-012, the closed-loop CARPENTER_HANDOFF.md hand-off, the Job Code paragraph-ID echo discipline, and the FEEDBACK-arrow-Foreman line. All of those collapsed into one section titled 'The Reinforcing Loop — one file, two hooks, nothing else' that names .carpenter/session.json as the single carpenter communication channel with the SessionStart hook reading it and the Stop hook archiving plus pushing it. A new subsection documents the session.json schema field by field so the next carpenter knows exactly what to write. The top-of-file 'Comms protocol' summary was rewritten to point at the same loop instead of the deleted in-flight.jsonl event stream. The 'Agent roles' line lost the Foreman entry because the Foreman doesn't drive briefs into this repo anymore under the new doctrine. The 'Dispatched session protocol' section was kept but renamed to 'Dispatch / sandbox-mode protocol' and pruned of references to the deleted three-section report and the gate_failed event, keeping the PFOR-016 dispatch-branch refspec discipline that the close.sh hook actually depends on. Repo Lock Protocol, Branch protocol, Quality gates, Manifest doctrine, the Doctrine Quintet read-first, PFOR-018 one-block-prose, PFOR-019 chip-form, LIVING-IDEAS, and Eyes-Payload were all kept verbatim or close to it because they describe behaviors that survive comms v2. Second, scripts/session-start-grounding.mjs and scripts/session-stop-gate.mjs were deleted from disk via git rm. The grounding script had been redundant since the migration commit added the bash session-start.sh hook, and the stop-gate had been retired from the Stop chain last session because it raced fatally with close.sh; both were dead weight. Third, CARPENTER_HANDOFF.md was deleted from the repo root. The file was structurally superseded by session.json the moment comms v2 landed, and leaving the prior letter on disk would only invite future drift back to the old loop. Fourth, .claude/settings.json was edited to drop the node session-start-grounding.mjs entry from the SessionStart hook chain so the now-deleted script is no longer referenced — only .claude/hooks/session-start.sh remains. UserPromptSubmit, Stop, and PreCompact blocks were left untouched. Fifth, .claude/hooks/session-close.sh got an archive-idempotency check: the hook now finds the latest archive file via 'ls -t' and uses 'cmp -s' to byte-compare it against the current session.json; if they match, the hook exits immediately. This closes the new spam-on-every-Stop behavior the prior carpenter surfaced — without the check, the timestamped archive name guaranteed a non-empty index diff per invocation and one checkpoint commit per Stop. After all five changes, the four gates were re-run end to end: typecheck silent pass, lint silent pass, 255 of 255 tests passing in 8.17 seconds, build clean with 356 modules transformed in 3.54 seconds. The deletions touched no source code and the doctrine rewrite was a markdown-only change, so test outcomes were never expected to shift; running them was the discipline, not the discovery.
narrative.whats_pending: One remaining hygiene question the operator may want to answer next: the appcommander/ folder still has skeleton-bootstrap artifacts that don't belong to the new loop. Specifically appcommander/scripts/carp-loop, carp-mark-consumed, carp-poll-operator, and carp-say are the old AppCommander-polled loop-driving scripts the new doctrine has obsoleted; appcommander/peer-memory/carpenter-asks-of-foreman.md and foreman-asks-of-carpenter.md are the old peer-letter channel the session.json narrative now subsumes; appcommander/jobs/job-001.md is a stale skeleton-bootstrap job spec from 2026-05-21; appcommander/manifests/{auth,wallet-core,backup-recovery,wallet-bot,app-connections,_shared}.ts are stale duplicates of the live src/features/<slug>/manifest.ts files (the features-registry only imports from src/features/, not from appcommander/manifests/, so the appcommander copies have drifted into pure metadata). The only appcommander/ files that may still serve a purpose are DOCTRINE_MANIFEST.json (declares which skeleton-doctrine version this repo carries — AppCommander may consult this from origin to track skeleton versions across spawns) and cockpit-cards.json (likely consumed by the AppCommander cockpit for visibility). The carpenter held back on touching any of those in this commit because removal needs an operator decision: if AppCommander still polls those files from origin/main for cockpit display, removing them would silently break a surface the carpenter can't see. Worth a chip-form question if the operator wants to do another sweep — 'Remove all of appcommander/ except DOCTRINE_MANIFEST.json + cockpit-cards.json / Remove all of appcommander/ including those two / Leave appcommander/ alone'. Beyond that, the three Phase E4 feature follow-ups the older CARPENTER_HANDOFF.md letter had flagged are still on the table: Phase D charter-amendment chain, JoinOrgModal vouch-cosignature collection sub-flow, receiveSelfMembership orgSelfDecl-lookup centralization. Those are pure feature work, not hygiene.
narrative.what_you_could_do_better: Two honest notes for the operator's eyes. First, the archive-idempotency check in session-close.sh uses 'cmp -s' which is a byte-exact compare; if a future change adds non-deterministic content to session.json (like a timestamp field that auto-updates on every write), the idempotency check will never fire and the per-Stop checkpoint commit spam will return. The current schema is safe because the carpenter writes session.json as a deliberate act with stable content, but the failure mode is worth naming so a future schema change doesn't accidentally re-break the loop. A safer alternative would be hashing the narrative fields only (jq -r '.narrative' | sha256sum) and comparing that, but the byte-compare is simpler and works for the current schema. Second, the doctrine rewrite preserved the 'Dispatched session protocol' subsection under its new 'Dispatch / sandbox-mode' name because the PFOR-016 dispatch-branch refspec discipline is load-bearing for the comms-v2 close.sh hook in this exact execution environment, but the subsection still mentions a dispatch-carpenter.yml workflow that does not exist in this repo. That reference is harmless context for any spawn that DOES have such a workflow, but for tapit-wallet specifically the truth is that we run in a managed remote execution environment (the Claude Code on the web container), which behaves identically to the GitHub Actions dispatch sandbox for PFOR-016 purposes. The current wording covers both cases generically by saying 'a sandbox where the origin/main checkout is a provisioning snapshot' — that's accurate but a future carpenter looking only for 'dispatch-carpenter.yml' in this repo will be briefly puzzled before realizing the same rules apply.
narrative.bigger_picture: Comms v2 finished landing today. The migration commit shipped last session, the dispatch-sandbox push patch and the stop-gate retirement landed in two follow-up commits, and this session closed the hygiene debt that was always going to follow: the old doctrine in CLAUDE.md, the dead scripts on disk, the orphaned CARPENTER_HANDOFF.md, and the per-Stop archive spam. The loop is now actually what the operator described in his voice paragraph — one SessionStart hook that grounds, one Stop hook that pushes, one file (.carpenter/session.json) that carries everything the next carpenter needs to know and everything AppCommander needs to display. The reduction from five comms files plus a CARPENTER_HANDOFF.md letter plus two .mjs hook scripts plus a sprawling doctrine block to one JSON file plus two bash hooks plus a focused doctrine is the kind of consolidation that tends to feel underwhelming in the moment because no new feature shipped, but the carpenter-loop is the substrate on which every future cut in this repo depends. A simpler, more honest loop means less ceremony cost per session, less drift between what the doctrine claims and what the code does, and less surface area for the same bug class that produced last session's infinite Stop-fire loop. The same pattern probably wants to ride into the AppCommander-side skeleton template so future spawns inherit the simpler loop rather than re-implementing the five-file protocol and then having to migrate out of it the way this repo just did. Worth flagging to the AppCommander operator: the COMMS_V2_AND_ADMIN_PAGE_SHIFT.md plan should now include 'rewrite skeleton CLAUDE.md doctrine to describe comms v2' and 'strip session-start-grounding.mjs and session-stop-gate.mjs from skeleton-bundled scripts' as concrete checklist items the AppCommander side has to land before the next spawn-from-skeleton happens, or every new spawn will start its life in the same five-file-protocol world this one just escaped.
